response: Hepatitis G virus and TT virus are not involved in cryptogenic chronic liver disease. According to studies, hepatitis G virus infection is widespread among patients with chronic hepatitis in Southern Italy, but its frequency in subjects with cryptogenic liver disease is similar to that in hepatitis C virus chronic liver disease, suggesting that hepatitis G virus does not play a causative role. Additionally, TT virus infection is uncommon in patients with cryptogenic or hepatitis C virus-related liver disease who do not have a history of parenteral exposure, further indicating that TT virus is not a significant factor in cryptogenic chronic liver disease.
